items.grounds: CONFIRM at medium. Re-derived from bytes both ways. The inventory the row names (prov_device_inventory.json bni_address) declares its count object as verses containing the word-bound vocative token, any position, pointed tier, count 22, by_chapter 3:3 and 4:2; its refs inside Prov.3.1-Prov.4.27 are Prov.3.1, Prov.3.11, Prov.3.21, Prov.4.10 and Prov.4.20 - five - so the row's 'first of four bni_address occurrences within the part' and 'four heading this part' misreport the very object they cite. Independent sweep over verse_map_oshb.json (word-bound skeleton token בני, classified by the vowel under the nun at pointed tier): 22 vocative verses / 22 tokens, one per verse, in two attested spellings, בְּ֭נִי (oshb:Prov.3.1, word 1) and בְנִ֣י (oshb:Prov.5.20, word 3), plus 8 tsere-construct verses / 8 tokens, matching the inventory exactly; the row's '22 tokens book-wide' therefore coincides numerically only because every vocative verse carries one token - the inventory's unit is verses. The omitted verse stands at word 3 of oshb:Prov.3.11, מוּסַ֣ר יְ֭הוָה בְּנִ֣י (byte tier), which the row's 'recurring at 3.21, 4.10, and 4.20' skips; the row's list would be right only under an unnamed opening-position object (word 1 at Prov.3.1, Prov.3.21 and Prov.4.20; word 2 at Prov.4.10, שְׁמַ֣ע בְּ֭נִי, byte tier), while it cites the any-position inventory. Not load-bearing, hence medium not high: word 1 of oshb:Prov.3.1 is בְּ֭נִי (byte tier); pmarks_Prov.json (WLC, single witness) carries PE at Prov.3.4 and PE at Prov.2.22, tier-3 weak corroboration only; word-bound יהוה tokens number 0 in Prov.3.1-Prov.3.4 and 5 across Prov.3.5-Prov.3.12 (one each at Prov.3.5, Prov.3.7, Prov.3.9, Prov.3.11, Prov.3.12), so the divine-name contrast is byte-true. Both sides of each seam weighed: front seam Prov.2.22|Prov.3.1 - the preceding unit closes on the third-person antithetic line וּ֭רְשָׁעִים מֵאֶ֣רֶץ יִכָּרֵ֑תוּ (oshb:Prov.2.22, byte tier) under the PE at Prov.2.22, and the row opens on the vocative, so the C1 vocative-plus-parashah rule decides it (exact skeleton-token overlap 0); rear seam Prov.3.4|Prov.3.5 - the row closes on בְּעֵינֵ֖י אֱלֹהִ֣ים וְאָדָֽם (oshb:Prov.3.4, byte tier) under the PE at Prov.3.4, and the next unit opens בְּטַ֣ח אֶל יְ֭הוָה (oshb:Prov.3.5, byte tier) with no vocative, so that seam rests on the parashah corroboration plus the byte-true naming shift, coherently with the following row, which carries the PE at Prov.3.10 inside its own span on the same naming-density ground. The register arm (part talk and an inventory name in row prose) is real and rides at low inside this medium. Repair validated: the proposed wording is byte-sound except that Prov.4.10's vocative is word 2, not verse-initial - restate the object either as opening-position vocative (word 1 or 2; 4 across the listed verses) or as the inventory's any-position verse count (5 across Prov.3-4, 22 book-wide), naming which.

CONFIRM at medium. Re-derived from bytes: pmarks_Prov.json (WLC, single witness) marks PE at Prov.3.18 and PE at Prov.3.35 with no parashah entry between them, no paseq entry in Prov.3.21-Prov.3.26 (the chapter's one paseq is at Prov.3.28) and no K/Q entry there (chapter K/Q at Prov.3.15, Prov.3.27, Prov.3.28, Prov.3.30, Prov.3.34), so the row's absence statement is byte-true - and the strategy's parashah rule (tier-3 weak; absence never counterevidence), repeated in the inventory's own marks_note, bars converting it into a ground against the rival, which the rejected_alternative does as its first-listed reason ('lacks any parashah or disclosure-object support'). The inadmissible ground is also non-discriminating: the row's own close after Prov.3.26 has no parashah support either (the same PE pair at Prov.3.18 and Prov.3.35 brackets both cuts), so the absence argument would count equally against the shipped bound. Not load-bearing, hence medium: the second ground is positive and byte-true - the second-person self-directed object runs through both halves of the rival's cut, אִם תִּשְׁכַּ֥ב לֹֽא תִפְחָ֑ד and וְ֝שָׁכַבְתָּ֗ וְֽעָרְבָ֥ה שְׁנָתֶֽךָ at oshb:Prov.3.24, אַל תִּ֭ירָא at oshb:Prov.3.25, בְכִסְלֶ֑ךָ and רַגְלְךָ֣ at oshb:Prov.3.26 (all byte tier) - and the row's own edges stand: word 1 of oshb:Prov.3.21 is בְּ֭נִי (byte tier) and oshb:Prov.3.27 opens אַל תִּמְנַע ט֥וֹב מִבְּעָלָ֑יו (byte tier), shifting the object to a third party. Both sides of every seam weighed: front seam Prov.3.20|Prov.3.21 - the wisdom poem closes on the third-person cosmic couplet בְּ֭דַעְתּוֹ תְּהוֹמ֣וֹת נִבְקָ֑עוּ (oshb:Prov.3.20, byte tier) and the row opens on the vocative, so the C1 vocative rule decides (exact skeleton-token overlap 0); rear seam Prov.3.26|Prov.3.27 - the row closes on כִּֽי יְ֭הוָה יִהְיֶ֣ה בְכִסְלֶ֑ךָ (oshb:Prov.3.26, byte tier) with the addressee's own confidence as object, and the following unit opens the prohibition series with a third-party object, so the addressee-object shift decides (overlap 0), coherently with the following row, which argues the same seam from the same shift; the rival's interior cut Prov.3.24|Prov.3.25 - the sleep couplet closes on וְ֝שָׁכַבְתָּ֗ וְֽעָרְבָ֥ה שְׁנָתֶֽךָ and the fear couplet opens אַל תִּ֭ירָא מִפַּ֣חַד פִּתְאֹ֑ם (oshb:Prov.3.25, byte tier), and a root-level catchword straddles that cut, תִפְחָ֑ד (oshb:Prov.3.24, word 4) against מִפַּ֣חַד (oshb:Prov.3.25, word 3), byte tier, one root in two distinct tokens (exact-token overlap 0), which under the cross-seam cohesion rule argues continuity across the rival's cut - positive byte evidence the row could have used in place of the absence. Repair validated as proposed: rest the rival's rejection on the shared second-person self-directed object alone and keep the in-span absence sentence as disclosure; the straddling root may be added only as root-level (not exact-token) support. The register defect on 'the part's second lecture-opening slot' is real and stays at low.

CONFIRM at medium. Re-derived from bytes: all four verses the row lists carry the singular vocative at pointed tier - word 1 of oshb:Prov.3.1 בְּ֭נִי, word 1 of oshb:Prov.3.21 בְּ֭נִי, words 1-2 of oshb:Prov.4.10 שְׁמַ֣ע בְּ֭נִי, word 1 of oshb:Prov.4.20 בְּ֭נִי (all byte tier) - so 'the singular address term shared by 3 of 4 lecture-openers in this part (3.1, 3.21, 4.10, 4.20)' contradicts its own enumeration: 4 of 4. The only object under which a 3-of-4 digit is true is verse-initial position (word 1 at Prov.3.1, Prov.3.21 and Prov.4.20; word 2 at Prov.4.10), an object the row never names and which its wording ('address term shared by') does not describe; against the inventory's any-position object (prov_device_inventory.json bni_address, count 22, by_chapter 3:3 and 4:2) the range Prov.3.1-Prov.4.27 holds five vocative verses, Prov.3.11 included at word 3 (מוּסַ֣ר יְ֭הוָה בְּנִ֣י, oshb:Prov.3.11, byte tier). A false digit, not alone load-bearing, hence medium: the seam's actual warrant is the plural address שִׁמְע֣וּ בָ֭נִים (oshb:Prov.4.1, words 1-2, byte tier) against those singular openers, byte-true whatever the tally. Both sides of both seams weighed: front seam Prov.3.35|Prov.4.1 - the preceding unit closes on the third-person antithetic line כָּ֭בוֹד חֲכָמִ֣ים יִנְחָ֑לוּ (oshb:Prov.3.35, byte tier) under the PE at Prov.3.35 (pmarks_Prov.json, tier-3 weak, single witness), and the row opens on the plural vocative, so the C1 vocative rule decides with parashah corroboration (exact skeleton-token overlap 0), coherently with the preceding row, which closes itself at that mark; rear seam Prov.4.4|Prov.4.5 - the row's last verse carries the speech frame וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לִ֗י (oshb:Prov.4.4, words 2-3, byte tier) and the first quoted line יִֽתְמָךְ דְּבָרַ֥י לִבֶּ֑ךָ שְׁמֹ֖ר מִצְוֺתַ֣י וֶֽחְיֵֽה (words 4-9, byte tier), and the next unit opens קְנֵ֣ה חָ֭כְמָה קְנֵ֣ה בִינָ֑ה (oshb:Prov.4.5, byte tier), an imperative pair inside the same quoted speech, with no vocative, no parashah entry, no paseq and no K/Q anywhere in Prov.4.1-Prov.4.4 (nearest K/Q at Prov.4.16, next PE at Prov.4.19) and overlap 0, so that seam rests on the speech-frame device alone - which the row discloses, and the following row records that it inherits the frame from Prov.4.4; medium_low with the frontier flag is therefore calibrated and the lowband disposition (not a defect) stands. The register arm ('in this part', 'this part's rows') is real, low. Repair validated with one correction: the proposed '4 of 4 verse-initial openers' is itself wrong for Prov.4.10 (word 2); restate as opening-position vocative (word 1 or 2), 4 of 4 across the listed verses, or as the inventory's any-position verse count, 5 across Prov.3-4.

CONFIRM at medium; span ruling endorse_proposal, qualified below. Re-derived from bytes both ways. The seam: oshb:Prov.6.23 opens on the motive particle כִּ֤י נֵ֣ר and oshb:Prov.6.24 opens on the purpose infinitive לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ מֵאֵ֣שֶׁת רָ֑ע (both byte tier), a lamed-infinitive with no finite clause of its own that hangs on what precedes - the row concedes this in its own rationale - and the seam carries neither ruled C1 signal: the chapter's word-bound vocative tokens stand at Prov.6.1 (word 1), Prov.6.3 (word 4) and Prov.6.20 (word 2, נְצֹ֣ר בְּ֭נִי, byte tier), none at Prov.6.24, and pmarks_Prov.json (WLC, single witness) carries PE at Prov.6.5, Prov.6.11, Prov.6.15, Prov.6.19, Prov.6.26 and Prov.6.35 - stated as inventory facts, never as absence-counterevidence. Exact skeleton-token overlap across Prov.6.23|Prov.6.24 is 0, so the seam rests on topic onset alone inside an argument that itself asserts syntactic continuity across it. Independent evidence the auditor did not cite settles the structure: the same purpose infinitive opens oshb:Prov.7.5, לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ מֵאִשָּׁ֣ה זָרָ֑ה (byte tier; word-bound sweep of the token לשמרך: 2 verses book-wide, Prov.6.24 and Prov.7.5, the two tokens byte-identical), and there it CLOSES the exordium (Prov.7.1 בְּ֭נִי שְׁמֹ֣ר אֲמָרָ֑י through Prov.7.5) before the narrative opens at oshb:Prov.7.6 with כִּ֭י בְּחַלּ֣וֹן בֵּיתִ֑י (byte tier); likewise oshb:Prov.5.2 לִשְׁמֹ֥ר מְזִמּ֑וֹת closes the Prov.5.1 vocative exordium before oshb:Prov.5.3 opens כִּ֤י נֹ֣פֶת (byte tier), and oshb:Prov.2.16 לְ֭הַצִּ֣ילְךָ מֵאִשָּׁ֣ה זָרָ֑ה (byte tier) is the same purpose clause inside the chapter-length lecture. The book's own lecture template binds the keep-you-from-the-woman purpose clause to the preceding exordium, so the shipped Prov.6.23|Prov.6.24 seam cuts the template's own join; the rival's rejection is circular exactly as filed (the 6:26-corroborated split is refused on the strength of the 6:24 infinitive the row concedes depends on 6:23). Not high: nothing the row states is byte-false, the unit it draws has real internal glue (the woman-noun spine מֵאֵ֣שֶׁת רָ֑ע at oshb:Prov.6.24, וְאֵ֥שֶׁת אִ֑ישׁ at oshb:Prov.6.26, אֵ֣שֶׁת רֵעֵ֑הוּ at oshb:Prov.6.29, byte tier), and the placement is one of two defensible cuts, so the defect is a seam warrant, not a byte-false load-bearing claim. Both sides at the proposed seam Prov.6.26|Prov.6.27: oshb:Prov.6.26 is a complete motive clause, כִּ֤י בְעַד אִשָּׁ֥ה זוֹנָ֗ה through נֶ֖פֶשׁ יְקָרָ֣ה תָצֽוּד (byte tier), closing under the PE at Prov.6.26 (tier-3 weak, single witness, corroboration only); oshb:Prov.6.27 opens a new construction, the interrogative הֲיַחְתֶּ֤ה אִ֓ישׁ (byte tier), whose paired question at oshb:Prov.6.28 (אִם יְהַלֵּ֣ךְ אִ֭ישׁ) is answered by כֵּ֗ן הַ֭בָּא at oshb:Prov.6.29 (byte tier) - a self-contained question-question-application figure. One straddle must be disclosed by any replacement warrant: the exact skeleton token איש stands at word 9 of oshb:Prov.6.26 (וְאֵ֥שֶׁת אִ֑ישׁ) and word 2 of oshb:Prov.6.27 (אִ֓ישׁ), a high-frequency noun (word-bound sweep: 53 verses book-wide) that is 'another man' inside the wife-phrase at 6:26 and the generic subject of the questions at 6:27-28, a weak lexical straddle outweighed by the syntactic dependency the shipped seam cuts. Both sides at the erased seam: Prov.6.23 closes no unit by any ruled device (no vocative, no mark, no refrain; its close וְדֶ֥רֶךְ חַ֝יִּ֗ים תּוֹכְח֥וֹת מוּסָֽר completes the lamp metaphor and the dependent infinitive follows), so the proposal meets the both-sides law. Qualifications on the proposal: (1) the endorsed route is the seam relocation, giving M8-Prov-026 = Prov.6.20-Prov.6.26 (onset on the vocative at word 2 of Prov.6.20 under the PE closing Prov.6.19; close on the PE-corroborated motive clause) and M8-Prov-027 = Prov.6.27-Prov.6.29 - one edit, ruled coherently for both rows; (2) the merge alternative Prov.6.20-Prov.6.29 is not endorsed, since it would bury the one parashah-corroborated interior seam the C1 rule names; (3) the proposal's 'both units sit inside the ~4-8 verse C1 range' is wrong for Prov.6.27-Prov.6.29 (3 verses) - that unit stands on its own construction, not on length; (4) the rear seam Prov.6.29|Prov.6.30 (closing לֹ֥א יִ֝נָּקֶ֗ה at oshb:Prov.6.29; oshb:Prov.6.30 opening לֹא יָב֣וּזוּ לַ֭גַּנָּב, byte tier; overlap only the negative particle; no mark, no vocative) is untouched by the proposal and outside this ruling. Everything here remains a PROPOSAL for the owner remediation docket; nothing is adopted.

CONFIRM at medium. Re-derived with the object named (sweep.py --skel, verse counts, plus word-bound token sweeps over verse_map_oshb.json): contiguous skeleton ברכה = 3 verses (Prov.10.7, Prov.11.25, Prov.11.26), the row's digit and set exactly; ברכת = 3 verses (Prov.10.22, Prov.11.11, Prov.24.25), the construct set the row discloses; ברכות = 2 verses (Prov.10.6, Prov.28.20), undisclosed; the root string ברכ = 8 verses, every hit a form of the same noun (per-verse tokens ברכות, לברכה, ברכת, בברכת, ברכה, וברכה, ברכת, ברכות; no verb or knee false hit, final-kaf allography excluded), so the auditor's digits are byte-true. The omitted set holds the nearest parallel to the row's own evidence: oshb:Prov.10.6 opens בְּ֭רָכוֹת לְרֹ֣אשׁ צַדִּ֑יק and oshb:Prov.11.26 closes וּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה לְרֹ֣אשׁ מַשְׁבִּֽיר (both byte tier), the same blessing-on-the-head construction with the byte-identical token לְרֹ֣אשׁ. A further byte fact strengthens the finding: at the lexeme level where 'the noun's rarity' is claimed, Prov.10.6|Prov.10.7 is a second ADJACENT pair of the noun (בְּ֭רָכוֹת at oshb:Prov.10.6 against לִבְרָכָ֑ה at oshb:Prov.10.7, byte tier), and that pair shares two exact skeleton tokens (צדיק, רשעים) where Prov.11.25|Prov.11.26 shares none (forms בְּרָכָ֥ה and וּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה, byte tier, unequal at every tier), so the row's 'this pair alone stands adjacent among them' is true only for the 3-verse spelling object it names and would be false for the noun. Why medium and not high: the rarity leg is unquantified rather than byte-false (8 verses of 915 is genuinely infrequent), the exclusivity claim is object-scoped and true at its named object, and the cluster's edges do not rest on it - exact-token overlap Prov.11.24|Prov.11.25 = 0 and Prov.11.26|Prov.11.27 = 0, neither neighbor carries any form of the noun, and pmarks_Prov.json records no mark, paseq or K/Q in Prov.11.24-Prov.11.27. Both sides weighed: front seam Prov.11.24|Prov.11.25 - oshb:Prov.11.24 closes its existential saying on וְחוֹשֵׂ֥ךְ מִ֝יֹּ֗שֶׁר אַךְ לְמַחְסֽוֹר and oshb:Prov.11.25 opens נֶֽפֶשׁ בְּרָכָ֥ה (byte tier), a new subject, coherently with the preceding row, which refuses extension on the same noun ground (byte-true); rear seam Prov.11.26|Prov.11.27 - oshb:Prov.11.26 closes on וּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה לְרֹ֣אשׁ מַשְׁבִּֽיר and oshb:Prov.11.27 opens שֹׁ֣חֵֽר ט֭וֹב (byte tier), a new seek/find subject, coherently with the following row. Under the C2 single-proverb default the cluster stands on a lexeme-level catchword (0 exact tokens) plus the giving/withholding pattern, the sub-two-token class the strategy expects at low confidence, so medium_low with the frontier flag is calibrated and the lowband disposition stands. Repair validated: the proposal's digits are byte-true; add to it that the 'alone adjacent' claim must be restated as spelling-scoped, or extended to disclose the Prov.10.6|Prov.10.7 adjacent pair, before the rarity leg can stand.

DOWNGRADE high to medium; span ruling decline_proposal for the split, with the restatement route endorsed as the repair. Re-derived from bytes: the two forms are וּלְשׁ֖וֹן (oshb:Prov.12.18, word 5 of 7) and לְשׁ֣וֹן (oshb:Prov.12.19, word 7 of 8), byte tier, unequal at byte, NFD, accent_stripped and skeleton tiers (skeletons ולשון against לשון, the conjunction prefix breaking the identity); exact skeleton-token overlap Prov.12.18|Prov.12.19 = 0; word-bound token ולשון = 3 verses (Prov.10.31, Prov.12.18, Prov.25.15), word-bound token לשון = 12 verses, contiguous substring לשון = 16 verses - three different objects, none named by the row. So the auditor is right that 'the exact same noun ... byte tier', 'exact skeleton token ... repeated' and 'one content token' are false at the token tier they name, and that the waw prefix is nowhere disclosed. Why not high: the fact the warrant rests on - the noun for tongue standing in both adjacent verses - is byte-true at lexeme tier (both quoted forms are exact byte splices at their refs and visibly differ by the prefix), and the book's cluster bar does not require exact shared tokens: the strategy admits proverb_cluster on byte-grounded cohesion evidence named in the rationale (a catchword chain among the named classes) and places catchword clusters thinner than two shared content tokens in the expected-low-confidence class, while the exact-token adjacency figure is a staged texture signal, never row evidence; the corpus's own sibling at Prov.11.25-Prov.11.26 ships on exactly this class (בְּרָכָ֥ה against וּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה, byte tier, 0 exact tokens) with the prefix disclosed, at medium_low. The boundary therefore survives a restated warrant; the defect is a tier overclaim plus an undisclosed prefix on the load-bearing warrant - a defective warrant statement, medium. The lowband trigger resolves the same way: medium_low with the frontier flag is the calibrated band for a one-lexeme catchword, and the row's comparison class is imprecise rather than false - Prov.13.19|Prov.13.20 shares the exact skeleton token כסילים (כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים at oshb:Prov.13.19 against כְסִילִ֣ים at oshb:Prov.13.20, byte tier, accents differ), this row shares a lexeme only. Both sides weighed under the C2 default: front seam Prov.12.17|Prov.12.18 - oshb:Prov.12.17 closes on וְעֵ֖ד שְׁקָרִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה and oshb:Prov.12.18 opens יֵ֣שׁ בּ֭וֹטֶה (byte tier), overlap 0, coherently with the preceding row's no-shared-lexeme rejection (byte-true); rear seam Prov.12.19|Prov.12.20 - oshb:Prov.12.19 closes on לְשׁ֣וֹן שָֽׁקֶר and oshb:Prov.12.20 opens מִ֭רְמָה בְּלֶב (byte tier), overlap 0, coherently with the following row. Texture noted, not ruled: a non-adjacent deceit web spans Prov.12.17-Prov.12.20 (שְׁקָרִ֣ים at oshb:Prov.12.17 against שָֽׁקֶר at oshb:Prov.12.19, root-level; מִרְמָֽה at oshb:Prov.12.17 against מִ֭רְמָה at oshb:Prov.12.20, the same skeleton token), straddling neither seam; the row discloses the falsehood-root part of it. pmarks_Prov.json: no mark, paseq or K/Q at Prov.12.17-Prov.12.20. Span ruling: the split into Prov.12.18-Prov.12.18 and Prov.12.19-Prov.12.19 is declined because its sole premise - that the bar demands exact shared tokens - is not the book's rule; the field repair is the sound route: restate at lexeme tier, disclose the waw-prefixed form at Prov.12.18 against the bare form at Prov.12.19, and name the three digits and objects above; observed_substrate_signals, strongest_rejected_alternative and confidence re-open with it. A PROPOSAL only; should the owner instead rule the cluster bar to exact shared tokens, the split follows and this ruling is conditional on that bar.

CONFIRM at medium. Re-derived from bytes (exact skeleton tokens from verse_map_oshb.json word splits): Prov.14.12|Prov.14.13 share one token, וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ (oshb:Prov.14.12, word 6) and וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ (oshb:Prov.14.13, word 5), byte tier, unequal at byte (accents differ) and equal at accent_stripped and skeleton tiers - the row's 'byte tier' is a splice-accuracy label, not an identity claim, and the identity holds one tier down; that token is the row's whole lexical glue. Prov.14.13|Prov.14.14 ALSO share exactly one token, and it is stronger on the bytes: לֵ֑ב (oshb:Prov.14.13, word 4) and לֵ֑ב (oshb:Prov.14.14, word 4) are byte-IDENTICAL, both carrying the atnach, i.e. both A-colon-final - slot-parallel in the same way the row's hinge word is B-colon-initial in both its verses. Neither this row nor the Prov.14.14 row discloses it, so the standing cross-seam rule (a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed) is breached at the row's forward edge.
